_comment: The sweep steps that have moved to Rust (ADR-0001), each with the order and failure policy
it had as a Python command module (ORDER, SWEEP, ADR-0014). The sweep merges these into its
plan without running anything (plexdb/rust.py), so a missing or broken plexdb-rs fails only
its own steps, each under its policy. plexdb-rs runs every name here
(crates/plexdb/src/steps.rs); its test checks that it has one for each.
fold-merge-decisions, fold-role-decisions, fold-name-decisions: right after migrate and in that
order, for the same reason as fold-list-decisions; best-effort for the same reason.
enrich-tmdb-keywords (50), enrich-tmdb-language (51), enrich-tmdb-edges (55): the TMDB sweeps, in
the places they had; best-effort because TMDB is an optional source (ADR-0004) and staleness
gating means a skipped pass costs nothing but freshness.
migrate: first, because every later step writes the schema it leaves; required, because a
sweep against a store this build cannot open has nothing to walk into.
fold-list-decisions: right after fold-name-decisions, because a sweep starts by applying what
a person decided since the last one; best-effort, because a malformed file costs the sweep
one step's report, not a night's library read.
enrich-anilist, enrich-letterboxd, enrich-wikidata (56): the optional keyword sources, after both
TMDB sweeps and before refresh-map draws from the keywords; equal numbers run by name.
enrich-mdblist-ratings (60): beside harvest-mdblist, which draws on the same daily quota, and
just before it by name; ratings are not keywords, so nothing waits on them. All four are
best-effort because each source is optional (ADR-0004) and a skipped pass costs only freshness.
harvest-mdblist, harvest-letterboxd-lists, harvest-mdblist-search: the last of the sources,
because a list entry can only resolve to a title walk already wrote; best-effort, because the
lists are staleness-gated and a missed harvest is picked up by the next run (ADR-0004).
walk: required, because Plex is the one required dependency (ADR-0004) and a sweep that could
not read the library must not publish a snapshot built on what it managed to get.
media-walk: right after walk, whose rating-key map it reads; best-effort, because the tracks
are a fact about a title, not what the sweep publishes a library from.
repair-identities, repair-fs-identities: pointed at a problem a person has diagnosed, never
fired on a timer, so they are commands outside the sweep (ADR-0014).
fold-extras (24), extras-walk (25): the declared extras libraries, after walk and before
prune-frames (ADR-0030); best-effort, because they read folders on the media share, not Plex,
and a failed pass is repeated by the ten-minute tick (plexdb/extras_tick.py).
prune-frames: straight after walk and the identity repairs, the steps that decide which
item_ids exist; best-effort, because without PLEXDB_FRAMES_DIR it is skipped and a failure
leaves only rows that match no title.
ingest-plays: ahead of the enrichment block on purpose, because plays are the data no re-scan
reproduces and TMDB is re-fetchable, so a sweep killed partway has already banked them.
enrich-tautulli-plays: straight after ingest-plays, whose output it enriches; best-effort,
because Tautulli is an optional adapter (ADR-0004) and its absence costs a sweep only the IP,
completion and paused-time columns.
prune-keyword-verdicts (63), film-suffix-verdicts (64), judge-keyword-pairs (65),
judge-keyword-roles (66): after every writer that stores keywords and before publish, in the
order they had; best-effort because Jev and the embedding server are optional services
(ADR-0004) and a pair or keyword is judged once and kept, so a skipped pass costs only the
rows it would have added.
check-files (22): straight after media-walk (21), which writes the parts it reads, and before
record-panels so a panel counting file verdicts sees tonight's; best-effort, because a verdict
is a fact about a file, not something a library is published from.
record-panels (23): right after check-files, so a panel counting file verdicts sees tonight's;
best-effort, because a panel's history is a convenience for a chart, not something a library
is published from.
refresh-map (67), refresh-tagnetwork (68): after every keyword writer and both judges, so the
views draw the merges this sweep decided, and before publish, which snapshots what they
write; best-effort, because Plex DB-EX draws a missing or stale view live and a failed
refresh costs load time and nothing else.
publish (90): last, because it snapshots whatever the run produced; required, because a sweep
whose snapshot is not published has not done what the sweep is for.
harvest-frames: a command, not a step: `plexdb schedule` starts it when PLEXDB_FRAME_HOURS open
and it writes frames.db alone (ADR-0024), so no sweep runs it.
commands: moved to Rust but in no sweep, so they carry no order or policy.
